chapter: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
title: Playing the snail at the Casino de Paris
summary: From 1950 he played the escargot and a policeman in the Casino de Paris show and enjoyed the mannequins and dancers while keeping professionally away from them.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: We're talking -- I'm coming up on '50 -- from '52. Now, '50, I got a job, the man from the Casino de Paris, I got -- I was walking in the Casino de Paris also. My roll was doing many things. My initial role was I had the part of the escargot, the snail, and I was growling and all the beasts of the forest were following me, and they were those real pretty dancing girls.

And man, I had a ball. So now what was happening, because there's beauty all around me, and I was playing that I had a role of the police (inaudible) you know, speaking French, French-speaking role, and singing. I was singing, too. But my whole tour was about an hour. And I would go to the Ciral.

Now, the reason I stayed at the Casino de Paris so long was all those pretty women were there. "Oh, Jacques, oh, you play so nice." And the mannequins, I was right across from the mannequins, and see, they're nude. And they'd come in and they'd have, you know -- they'd have to shave all their hair off, off of their parts, you know.
Yeah. They had to have it -- strings looking like their body, put tape on it.
Oh, so they had like a flesh-colored G-string?

Yeah. So they were coming -- 'My husband, my boyfriends are not treating me right. I can't understand her's coming there as beautiful as can be. 'Fix this for me.' And (unintelligible). And beautiful, beautiful. They're beautiful people. All of them are beautiful. And then they had the dancers, then they had the ballet. Then they had the little dancers. And those little dancers are always got finished fighting fighting, going to get somebody. Everytime--they either/ or getting ready to fight somebody. And the mannequins were so beautiful, I used to look at them (inaudible) because they stood up and posed and everything. I had a number with them, too.

So I said to myself, now if I bother any of these women, they have a baby, they'll say, now, I told you--he's been in there. And they'd know I was (unintelligible). So I left them women alone. So the man says, well, Butler, you are a good worker. I said, why do you say that? He says, because you left my women alone. I said, that's why I come here for, to let them -- I didn't come here to get none of your women. Yeah.
